item.title: William Shatner and daughter Melanie recall fighting stage 4 cancer together
item.description: Actor William Shatner and his daughter, Melanie Shatner Gretsch, recall how they helped each other as they fought stage 4 cancer side by side.

item.title: Watch Live: Sen. Lindsey Graham remembered in Washington ceremonies today
item.description: President Trump is delivering a eulogy for Sen. Lindsey Graham, his one-time opponent for the presidency and later, his close ally.

item.title: eBay settles with couple "terrorized" in bizarre stalking scandal
item.description: eBay has agreed to pay a large settlement after a Massachusetts couple was the victim of a bizarre harassment campaign​.

item.title: Berlin Pride attacker was "hardcore ISIS sympathizer" on government list, extremism expert says
item.description: Authorities say the suspect who attacked Berlin's Pride event was known to German police for other crimes. Dr. Hans-Jakob Schindler of the Counter Extremism Project speaks on German efforts to monitor extremists, and CBS News' Bradley Blackburn takes a look at German data on hate crimes against LGBTQ+ people.

item.title: Fauci diaries, released by Sen. Paul, touch on COVID origins, Trump
item.description: Republican Sen. Rand Paul released more than a thousand pages of journal entries from Dr. Anthony Fauci, teeing up what is likely to be a contentious hearing on Wednesday.

item.title: Father of IDF soldier killed by Hamas shares memories of Lindsey Graham
item.description: Ruby Chen, the father of slain Israeli-American IDF soldier Itay Chen, shares his experiences with the late Sen. Lindsey Graham after the October 7, 2023, attacks.

item.title: Watch: Armed forces carry Lindsey Graham's casket into U.S. Capitol
item.description: Lindsey Graham's casket arrived at the U.S. Capitol as attendees pay their respects to the late senator. CBS News' Taurean Small has more on Graham's legacy.

item.title: The biggest weather risk for homeowners? It's no longer hurricanes.
item.description: Severe "convective" storms account for roughly a third of global natural disaster economic losses, a new study finds.

item.title: Trump to meet Netanyahu as his threat to resume strikes looms over Iran
item.description: Trump will meet Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu as the U.S. and Iran hold their fire amid work toward a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: People trapped and injured after powerful earthquake strikes Japan
item.description: A powerful earthquake hit southern Japan, seriously damaging a shopping mall where there are reportedly many people trapped and some dead.

item.title: Can you transfer a credit card balance if you've missed payments?
item.description: A balance transfer is a powerful tool to use for credit card debt, but missed payments can complicate the process.

item.title: Wildfires scorch Spain and France with more dry weather expected
item.description: Firefighters in Spain and France are battling some of the worst wildfires western Europe has ever seen with more hot and dry weather anticipated. Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Mornings Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Dozens injured, buildings damaged after powerful earthquake strikes Japan
item.description: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake rocked southern Japan on Tuesday, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency. Dozens of people are injured, officials say. Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: Woman murdered in 1936 and buried under building is finally identified
item.description: Police have finally identified the remains of a woman murdered nearly a century ago and buried beneath a building in Toronto.

item.title: William Shatner and his daughter open up about how they battled stage 4 cancer at the same time
item.description: Legendary actor William Shatner and his daughter Melanie Shatner Gretsch are opening up about their battles with stage 4 cancer nearly at the same time as each other. Both are now cancer-free and share how they helped each other through the challenging time.

item.title: Biden tells ghostwriter "some of this may be classified, be careful" in released audio tapes
item.description: After a long legal battle, the Department of Justice released audio recordings containing former President Joe Biden's discussions with his ghostwriter. Biden criticized the release of the audio tapes as "political retribution" by the Trump administration. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: Ariana Grande files lawsuit alleging hackers stole her unreleased music
item.description: In a new lawsuit, Ariana Grande alleges unidentified hackers caused "irreparable harm" to her career and stole her unreleased music, photos and videos. She's asking the court to force internet providers to identify them.

item.title: Bryan Kohberger challenges conviction in Idaho murders
item.description: Bryan Kohberger​, the man serving multiple life sentences for the murders of four University of Idaho students​, filed a petition for post-conviction relief Monday.

item.title: Bryan Kohberger files petition to take back guilty plea in Idaho murders
item.description: Bryan Kohberger, the man sentenced for the 2022 murders of four University of Idaho students, pleaded guilty last year as part of a deal. Now, he wants to take back his guilty plea and go to trial. Jericka Duncan reports.

item.title: Will tensions kill progress during Trump's meeting with Israel's Netanyahu?
item.description: President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu are set to meet as the war in Iran intensifies. CBS News' Courtney Kealy has more on what to expect.

item.title: People trapped in shopping mall rubble after strong 7.1 earthquake rattles Japan
item.description: A powerful 7.1-magnitude earthquake rocked southern Japan, destroying infrastructure, trapping people under rubble and causing injuries. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio has more as details emerge.

item.title: Haitian immigrant says "we are facing the worst" amid ICE deportation plan
item.description: As the Trump administration moves to deport Haitian immigrants, Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine, a Republican, is criticizing the president's plan. Camilo Montoya-Galvez spoke to the people at risk.

item.title: Biden tapes released after legal battle, with references to classified material
item.description: Audio recordings that former President Joe Biden fought for years to keep private have now been released.

item.title: Judge orders immigration officials to free key witness in deadly ICE shooting
item.description: A federal judge ordered U.S. immigration authorities to release a key witness in the fatal shooting of a Mexican homebuilder by a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in Houston.

item.title: Johnson & Johnson offers $5.5 billion to settle talc lawsuits
item.description: Johnson & Johnson has offered $5.5 billion to settle tens of thousands of lawsuits claiming its baby powder and other talcum powder products caused ovarian cancer, the company says.

item.title: In final debate, Michigan Senate Democrats spar over outside spending
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens clashed on outside spending and electability in their last debate before Michigan's Democratic primary next week.

item.title: Trump asks Supreme Court to step into dispute over mail-in ballots
item.description: A federal appeals court on Sunday left in place a lower court decision that blocked implementation of key parts of President Trump's executive order.

item.title: Carly Simon reveals Parkinson's diagnosis: "Learning how to live with it"
item.description: Carly Simon, the singer known for 1970s hits like "You're So Vain," announced she has Parkinson's disease and also was treated for basal cell carcinoma.

item.title: COVID-19 vaccines saved nearly 20 million lives in a year, study says
item.description: The researchers say 600,000 more deaths could have been prevented if vaccine roll-out had been more ubiquitous.
